newsitem.title: USA: San Diego County set to sell solid waste system.
newsitem.headline: San Diego County set to sell solid waste system.

text.p: San Diego County plans to sell its solid waste system in a bid to protect the county's general fund, ensure all debt holders are repaid, and cover future liabilities, county officials said on Wednesday.
The county Board of Supervisors has directed the county's chief administrative officer to develop a competitive process for sale of the system and its divestiture from the county.

"If you can sell off an asset that is not generating revenue you can work out a lot of debt, you can work off a lot of exposure and you can return money to the general fund," chief administrative officer Larry Prior said.
The county expects to take in between $100 million and $200 million on the sale. The money raised from the sale would be used to retire outstanding debt and cover liabilities.

Rating agency Moody's Investors Service Inc said it would review the county's plan. "It's certainly positive they have a plan to move forward and we want to evaluate the details of the plan," Moody's Vice President Nikolai Sklaroff said.

In a memoradum released Tuesday, Prior told county supervisors that the divestiture of the solid waste system was the most effective way to meet the "objectives of repaying indebtedness and insulating the general fund."

"An influx of funds from a system sale will not only allow repayment of the county's indebtedness, but will reassure the financial community, and reestablish the county's positive credit rating," Prior said in the memorandum.

The chief administrative officer said current economic and corporate conditions are "excellent" for the sale of the system. He added that government's public disclosure mandates and political pressure create difficulties for the county to compete in the volatile solid waste marketplace.
The county said the divestiture process would be lengthy.

The county's chief administrative office was given the authority to quickly hire consultants to work on the sale. Prior said he has already receiving letters from companies expressing interest in the system.

In October, Moody's cut San Diego County's debt ratings to a new low, warning that the southern California county's financial flexibility and credit position had weakened. Moody's lowered San Diego County long-term obligations to Baa1 from single-A.
